## UMAR {#umar}

### Urban microclimate-aware retrofitting framework for climate-resilient energy demand reduction

::: {.project-meta}
**Role:** Principal Investigator

**Funder:** [Energy Demand Research Centre](https://www.edrc.ac.uk/) (EDRC, funded by EPSRC/ESRC)

**Year:** 2025–2026
:::

UMAR investigated how urban microclimate can inform climate-resilient retrofit of social housing. Working with **Plymouth Community Homes**, we combined urban climate and building energy modelling to assess heating demand, summer overheating and retrofit options under current and future climates.

::: {.source-note}
[EDRC project overview](https://www.edrc.ac.uk/research/projects/urban-microclimate-aware-retrofitting-framework-for-climate-resilient-energy-demand-reduction-umar/) · [University project record](https://researchportal.plymouth.ac.uk/en/projects/urban-microclimate-aware-retrofitting-framework-for-climate-resil/).
:::

**Related research:** [Climate-resilient buildings and retrofit](../research/index.qmd#climate-resilient-retrofit).

### Increasing urban overheating risk from cooling decarbonisation by heat pumps {#heat-pump-overheating}

::: {.project-meta}
**Role:** Key Researcher (Postdoctoral Research Associate)

**Year:** 2023–2024

**Funding:** EPSRC, through the [H+C Zero Network](https://gtr.ukri.org/find-research-and-innovation/project/50d53f5a-e5e8-466a-97c6-cad12fe52c6e)
:::

The project examined how heat rejected during heat-pump cooling could affect urban microclimates and indoor heat exposure. [Cardiff University project overview](https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/research/explore/find-a-project/view/2806605-increasing-urban-overheating-risk-from-cooling-decarbonisation-by-heat-pumps).

**Related research:** [Heat pumps and urban energy exchange](../research/index.qmd#low-carbon-technologies).
